newsitem.title: USA: Fund-raisers fined at U.S. Agriculture Department.
newsitem.headline: Fund-raisers fined at U.S. Agriculture Department.

text.p: Four men involved in illegal political fund-raising at the Agriculture Department were sentenced Friday to two years' probation and ordered to pay modest fines.

U.S. Magistrate Patrick Attridge ordered two of the men, Jack Webb and Jeffress Wells, to serve 30 days in a halfway house. Webb and Wells allegedly prepared, at the request of a superior, lists of whom to reward and whom to punish in the department after President Clinton's election in 1992.
Prosecutor Laura Ingersoll declined to say if the Justice Department was still investigating the matter. "I cannot address that," she told reporters.

Webb, Wells and codefendants Jack Forlines and Grady Bilberry pleaded guilty in September to violating federal laws against politicking on the job. The men were supervisors in 1992 and solicited donations from underlings with the promise that the contributions would aid their careers if Clinton won.

Court documents said the fund-raising was coordinated with an outsider who later was appointed to a senior post at the Agriculture Department. An House Agriculture subcommittee identified that person as Grant Buntrock, chief of the Farm Service Agency, who has said he did nothing improper and political affiliation played no role in job assignments.

During a subcommittee hearing, Ron Blackley, chief of staff to former Agriculture Secretary Mike Espy, denied asking for lists of employees to be aided or blocked. A report by the subcommittee said people who contributed money were rewarded, while suspected Republican supporters were punished.

Attridge ordered Webb and Wells to pay $2,500 fines and perform 120 hours of community service each in addition to serving probation and time in a halfway house. Forlines and Bilberry were ordered to pay fines of $1,000 and to perform 100 hours each of community service in addition to probation.
All four apologised for their actions at the sentencing. Webb, Wells and Forlines have retired from federal work.
"As a child, I was taught my sins would be found out and punished. ... Mine have. I trust you will have mercy," Forlines said to Attridge.
